# Gmail Labels and Search Queries as Tabs

> A free Chrome extension (Manifest V3) that puts Gmail labels and saved
> searches in a tab bar above the inbox, with live unread counts, tab colours,
> separate configuration per Gmail account, and optional cleanup rules that run
> as a Google Apps Script in the user's own Google account.

Also known as: Gmail Labels as Tabs.

- Install: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/gmail-labels-and-search-q/jemjnjlplglfoiipcjhoacneigdgfmde
- Home: https://palworks.github.io/Gmail-Labels-As-Tabs/
- Privacy policy: https://palworks.github.io/Gmail-Labels-As-Tabs/#/privacy
- Terms: https://palworks.github.io/Gmail-Labels-As-Tabs/#/terms
- Changelog: https://palworks.github.io/Gmail-Labels-As-Tabs/#/changelog
- Support: https://palworks.github.io/Gmail-Labels-As-Tabs/#/contact
- Source: https://github.com/PalWorks/Gmail-Labels-Queries-As-Tabs

## Facts

Every line here can be checked against the public source repository.

- Free, MIT licensed, no account, no paid tier, no ads.
- Runs only on mail.google.com. Message content is never read, stored or
  transmitted.
- Permissions: storage, downloads, management, and the host mail.google.com.
  Each is used for one thing: saving tabs, writing an export file, and letting
  the in-app Uninstall button remove the extension.
- No analytics and no telemetry in the extension. One outbound request exists
  and only on a user action: the feedback form. A second page, a short
  uninstall survey, is opened by Chrome after removal and carries no identifier.
- Settings sync through Chrome's own sync, per Gmail account.
- "System" theme means Gmail's own theme, not the desktop's, because Gmail's
  theme is an account setting and the tab bar has to blend into the inbox.
- Cleanup rules never run on the publisher's side. The extension generates a
  Google Apps Script that the user pastes into their own account and schedules
  themselves. Mail is moved to Trash, where Gmail keeps it for 30 days.
- Current version: 1.6.2.

## Answers

Does it read my email? No. It reads label names and unread counts from the
Gmail page in the browser.

Does it work with multiple Gmail accounts? Yes. Each account keeps its own
tabs, colours, order and rules.

Is it free? Yes, and open source under the MIT license.

Does it work in Firefox or Safari? No. It is published for Chrome and runs in
Chromium browsers that install from the Chrome Web Store.
